ContactChange contains accountId, a committed contact snapshot (absent when deleted), and string kinds replacing .NET flags. Grant states use transaction-cached device states.
ContactChange.kinds represents relationship, alias, authorization and deleted as a string array.
ContactRequestChange carries accountId, direction, kind and the committed request snapshot. Removed requests omit request; delivery events preserve each committed send state.
ContactRequestChange.kind uses added, updated and removed. No request event is emitted for an absent dismissal or an unrelated protocol send.
GroupChange extends GroupInfo with kinds; committed page, nickname and local membership/status snapshots replace the nested .NET event wrapper. Ordinary messages do not emit groupChanged.
GroupChange.kinds represents properties, members, roles, bans, nickname and status. Verified management changes are combined per committed page.
Typed ConversationChange payload uses conversationId and kind created/updated/removed; notifications do not await application observers.
Typed ConversationChange payload uses conversationId and kind created/updated/removed; notifications do not await application observers.
AccountState uses the string states unknown, notEstablished and established.
BackgroundFailure carries operation, optional resource and the original unknown error. onLifecycle replaces the .NET event wrapper.
BackgroundFailure.operation is an open descriptive string, including observer diagnostics, rather than the three-value .NET enum.
ComponentState uses uninitialized, stopped, running, stopping and disposed string values.
ComponentEvents.stateChanged carries previous and current lifecycle states.
ChannelEvents.followChanged carries the full channel reference and isFollowed; channel.channelId is the .NET ChannelId equivalent.
ChannelPostChange carries ref, kind and optional info from the committed post projection.
ChannelPostChange.kind uses added, edited and deleted string values.
ChannelEvents.timelineChanged carries channel and a changes array.
DeviceAuthorizationState uses unknown, notRegistered, notYetValid, expired and authorized.
DeviceEvents.deviceChanged passes the device ID string directly.
GroupEvents.applicationsChanged passes the GroupRef directly.
GroupEvents.keyRecoveryChanged passes the GroupRef directly.

GroupEvents.timelineChanged emits one processed sequence with group and optional message. Filter for message to collect the .NET Messages-array equivalent; nickname/rejection progress may have no message.
MessageEvents.messageReceived passes the readonly MessageInfo array directly.
MessageEvents.sendStatusChanged passes MessageSendStatus directly.

DeviceSigner exposes certificate and asynchronous sign with optional AbortSignal.
RelayRegistry exposes context, getRelay and AsyncIterable getRelays. Missing entries use undefined.
SecretProtector provides asynchronous protect/unprotect with a purpose string and optional AbortSignal.
PublishDeviceStateOptions has previousState, recovery and revision; it also supports explicit certificates and signal.
DeviceStatePublishResult extends the validated accepted/staged response with deviceState.
DirectMessage is the structural draft passed to MessageManager.sendMessage, including body, attachments and replyTo.
MessageKey carries sender and messageId for persisted direct-message lookup.
GroupPageRequest has cursor/limit; channel history exposes the same fields as ChannelHistoryRequest.
GroupPage<T> carries readonly items and optional nextCursor; ChannelHistoryPage specializes the same shape for channel posts.
Structural request, explicit wire codec and accountAuthenticationInput replace the .NET instance signing helper.
Structural challenge, wire codec and validateChallenge; timestamps use integer Unix seconds.
Structural request, explicit wire codec and deviceAuthenticationInput replace the .NET instance signing helper.
Structural credentials, wire codec and validateSession, including token, mode and expiresAt.
SessionMode is the account/device string union.
DeviceStatePublishResponse.status is the accepted/staged string union.
RelayInfo has an explicit codec and validateRelayInfo; the descriptor may supply additional capability constraints.
RelayLimits has an explicit codec; numeric limits are validated by validateRelayInfo and discovery.
compareRoutes returns older, newer, equivalent or conflict.
RelayEntry retains relayId, endpoint, status and UInt64 updatedAt as bigint milliseconds.
RelayEntry.status is the active/disabled/suspended string union.

RelayAuthenticationState includes none, authenticating, account, device, expired and rejected. Rejection is independent of observer diagnostics and clears on new authentication; recoverable socket renewal errors can retain the accepted session.
RelayConnectionState uses disconnected, connecting and connected string values.
QueryReader<T> exposes readNext(count, signal) and dispose with fixed snapshot semantics; implementations validate counts and cancellation.

Neo identity uses getAccountId, validateAccountId and matchesAccount; raw signature verification is verifyAccount in crypto/primitives.ts. Identity-bound verification composes signature and identity checks. No adapter class/registry, protected subclass hooks or standalone generic CAIP-10 GetChainId equivalent is exported; this is not one-to-one utility API parity.
getRelayId, validateRelayId and verifyRelay provide relay identity operations; verifyAccount provides raw P-256 signature verification.
ClientOptions retains context/accountId and adds an injectable clock. Constructors validate arguments; no separate options.Validate method is exposed.
ProfileUpdate uses optional fields; null clears nickname/avatar/bio, while publicDiscovery accepts a boolean. Omission leaves a value unchanged.
CLR wrapper and implicit conversion are replaced by optional properties and null deletion in permitted update models. Complete documents use separate null rejection. No FieldUpdate class is exported.
Account/profile/device resolution uses validated account arguments and the { account } JSON query directly; no standalone AccountQuery class is required.
ContactRecord.status is the active/deleted string union, validated by contactRecordCodec.
DeviceManager validates the notification revision as a nonnegative safe integer before synchronization; raw notifications use RpcNotification and JsonObject rather than a separate DTO.

createIdentifier, validateIdentifier, deriveDeviceId and deriveResourceId consolidate per-kind helpers with a discriminant. certificateId in models/identity.ts derives a device ID from its certificate.
MessageDeliveryStatus.status uses delivering/target_accepted/failed wire values, distinct from local MessageSendState.

Readonly structural models, ExtensibleModel and explicit ProtocolCodec objects replace CLR inheritance and ToJson/FromJson. Semantic validation remains an explicit per-model function; the internal codec factory is not a public subclassing API.
Typed codecs preserve $type; signingInput and per-model input helpers apply network/domain separation and field exclusions. There is no public base-class constructor.
The wire model is RelayFailure with relayFailureCodec; retryAfter and rpcErrorCodes expose retry/code metadata. The JavaScript RelayError exception retains failure and isDefinitiveRejection.
The error payload is named RpcFailure. rpcFailureError maps recognized numeric codes to RelayError; unrecognized codes become ProtocolError('unknown_rpc_error'), rather than a nullable code lookup.

encodeRpcRequest validates and serializes outbound calls. Inbound notifications use RpcNotification. Request IDs and notification discrimination are represented structurally; no mutable RpcRequest DTO is exported.
decodeRpcMessage returns the discriminated RpcMessage success/failure variants; no response base class is exported.
RpcMessage with kind: success retains the request ID and JSON result.
RpcMessage with kind: failure retains ID (including null) and error. The TypeScript RpcFailure name instead denotes the inner error payload.

Channel publication validates the accepted sequence before persisting its acknowledgement; group operations also validate sequence results. The one-field reply is consumed as JsonObject rather than a separate exported DTO.
NodeSqliteStore accepts a filename; browser and Expo stores have platform-specific configuration. There is no shared .NET DatabaseOptions class or database-file compatibility promise.
MeshlineStore.migrate provides the explicit migration capability, implemented separately by each platform adapter. Initialization does not create a missing database.
EF Core Up/Down/model-builder hooks are CLR infrastructure, not TypeScript exports. Each adapter owns its schema/migrate implementation; .NET migration and database compatibility are not supported.
RelayError extends Error and retains the cloned RelayFailure, optional HTTP/RPC code, retry metadata and definitive-rejection classification.

Validators throw ProtocolError with a string code/message instead of returning a nullable violation record. Some argument errors use TypeError/RangeError. Exception behavior is an explicit language adaptation.
ProtocolError codes identify individual validation failures; the eight-value CLR classification enum is not separately exported. Codes are not a one-to-one rename of that enum.
